mainTopic: Making מצוה items: when a ברכה is said, who may make ציצית, preparing threads and dye לשמה, and checking תכלת
overview: The amud opens by finishing a challenge. תפילין written by a גוי are invalid, yet a Jew who writes תפילין says no ברכה. So the גמרא sets the real rule: a ברכה is said on making something only if the act itself completes the מצוה, like מילה, and not if it only prepares an item, like writing תפילין. It uses this rule to explain the argument about a ברכה on attaching ציצית: is ציצית an obligation on the garment or on the person? רב מרדכי then gives a version of רב's teaching in which ציצית made by a גוי are valid, learned from 'ועשו להם'. Next, רב and שמואל argue about which threads may be used for ציצית and whether the thread must be spun לשמה, an argument that matches an older dispute between תנאים about leather for תפילין. The גמרא describes how תכלת was dyed and learns rules from it: test-dyed wool is invalid because dyeing must be לשמה, and testing can ruin the dye, which is itself a dispute between תנאים. Finally, a ברייתא says תכלת cannot be checked and must be bought from an expert. The גמרא challenges this from רב יצחק, who did test תכלת, and the description of his test continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A ברייתא: sacred texts written by someone not obligated in תפילין are invalid
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that a ספר תורה, תפילין, or מזוזות written by a מין, כותי, גוי, slave, woman, minor, or משומד are invalid. Only someone included in tying on תפילין may write them.
steps.simpleTranslation: [As רב המנונא בר רבא] of Pashronya taught: A ספר תורה, תפילין, or מזוזות that were written by a heretic, a כותי, a גוי, a slave, a woman, a minor, or a Jewish apostate are invalid. The פסוק says 'And you shall tie them' and 'And you shall write them.' Anyone who is included in tying is included in writing. Anyone who is not included in tying is not included in writing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is in the middle of a challenge. It brings a ברייתא to prove one half of its point: תפילין written by a גוי are invalid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא puts two words of the פסוק side by side, 'tie them' and 'write them.' From this it learns that only people obligated in wearing תפילין may write them. This fact will be paired with the next step: a Jew who writes תפילין says no ברכה. Together, the two facts show that 'invalid when done by a גוי' does not lead to 'a Jew says a ברכה.'

keyTerms.meaning: A heretic, a Jew who rejects basic Torah beliefs
A Samaritan
A Jewish apostate who has abandoned Torah observance
Whoever is obligated in tying on תפילין may write them
Invalid, not usable for the מצוה

steps.confusionAlert: This text starts in the middle of a sentence. The first word, 'of Pashronya,' finishes the name of the sage who taught this ברייתא, from the line just before.

phrases.english: of Pashronya:
A Torah scroll, tefillin, or mezuzot

as it says: 'And you shall tie them' and 'And you shall write them,'

steps.triggerLanguage: מִפַּשְׁרוּנְיָא: סֵפֶר תּוֹרָה, תְּפִילִּין וּמְזוּזוֹת שֶׁכְּתָבָן מִין

steps.title: A Jew who writes תפילין says no ברכה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proves from רבי יוחנן that the ברכות on תפילין are said only when putting them on, not when making them. So a Jew who writes תפילין says no ברכה, even though תפילין written by a גוי are invalid.
steps.simpleTranslation: And a Jew does not need to say a ברכה. For רב חייא the son of רב הונא sent a ruling in the name of רבי יוחנן: On the arm תפילין one says 'Blessed... who made us holy with His מצוות and commanded us to put on תפילין.' On the head תפילין one says 'Blessed... who made us holy with His מצוות and commanded us about the מצוה of תפילין.' But one does not say a ברכה 'to make תפילין'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא completes its challenge. It proves that a Jew writing תפילין says no ברכה, because רבי יוחנן lists only the ברכות for putting them on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן gives a full list of the ברכות on תפילין. There is no ברכה of 'to make תפילין' on the list. So תפילין are invalid when made by a גוי, and still a Jew says no ברכה on making them. That breaks the earlier idea that 'invalid by a גוי' means 'a Jew says a ברכה.'

keyTerms.meaning: To put on תפילין, the ברכה on the arm תפילין
About the מצוה of תפילין, the ברכה on the head תפילין
To make תפילין, a ברכה that is NOT said
Whereas, but

phrases.english: And a Jew does not need to recite a blessing,

phrases.aramaic: דִּשְׁלַח רַב חִיָּיא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב הוּנָא
phrases.english: as Rav Chiyya the son of Rav Huna sent
in the name of Rabbi Yochanan:
On tefillin of the arm one says:
'Blessed... who sanctified us with His commandments
and commanded us to put on tefillin,'
On tefillin of the head one says:
'Blessed... who sanctified us with His commandments
and commanded us concerning the commandment of tefillin,'
whereas he does not recite 'to make tefillin'!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבְיִשְׂרָאֵל אֵין צָרִיךְ לְבָרֵךְ, דִּשְׁלַח רַב חִיָּיא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the second half of the challenge: invalid by a גוי (step 1), yet no ברכה for a Jew (this step).
steps.raayaObject: That a Jew who writes תפילין says no ברכה
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוחנן's list of ברכות on תפילין, which has no 'לַעֲשׂוֹת תְּפִילִּין'
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that whether a Jew says a ברכה depends on whether the item is valid when made by a גוי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: תפילין are invalid when made by a גוי, yet a Jew says no ברכה on making them, so validity by a גוי cannot be the deciding factor.

steps.title: The real rule: a ברכה is said only when the act completes the מצוה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives the true reason. If doing the act completes the מצוה, like מילה, a Jew says a ברכה even though a גוי's מילה is valid. If the act does not complete the מצוה, like writing תפילין, a Jew says no ברכה even though a גוי's writing is invalid.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, isn't this the reason: Any מצוה where doing the act is the completion of the מצוה, like מילה, even though it is valid when done by a גוי, a Jew must say a ברכה. And any מצוה where doing the act is not the completion of the מצוה, like תפילין, even though they are invalid when made by a גוי, a Jew does not need to say a ברכה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the 'valid by a גוי' idea and replaces it with a new test: does this act finish the מצוה or only prepare for it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Whether a גוי's act is valid has nothing to do with the ברכה. What matters is whether the act itself is the מצוה. Cutting the מילה is the מצוה itself. Writing תפילין only prepares the item, and the מצוה happens later when you put them on, which is when the ברכה is said.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, isn't this the reason, introducing the true explanation
The completion of the מצוה, the act that finishes it
Its making or doing
Circumcision
Valid

steps.whatToRemember: A ברכה on making something is said only if the making itself completes the מצוה (מילה). Preparing an item that will be used for the מצוה later (writing תפילין) gets no ברכה. Validity when done by a גוי is not the test.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think that writing תפילין is unimportant. It is required, and must be done by someone obligated. It simply isn't the moment the מצוה is completed, so no ברכה is said then.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a general principle for ברכות on making מצוה items, and the גמרא uses it right away to explain the argument about ציצית.

phrases.english: Rather, isn't this the reason:
any commandment whose performance is the completion of the commandment,
such as circumcision,
even though it is valid by a gentile,
a Jew must recite a blessing;

phrases.aramaic: וְכׇל מִצְוָה דַּעֲשִׂיָּיתָהּ לָאו גְּמַר מִצְוָה,
phrases.english: and any commandment whose performance is not the completion of the commandment,
such as tefillin,
phrases.notes: He means writing the תפילין. The מצוה is only completed when you put them on.

phrases.english: even though they are invalid by a gentile,
a Jew does not need to recite a blessing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of steps 1–2 by replacing the old test with a new one.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Replaces the proposed principle with a different underlying reason
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברכה depends on whether the act would be valid if done by a גוי.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברכה depends on whether the act itself completes the מצוה.

steps.title: The argument about ציצית: an obligation on the garment or on the person
steps.stepSummary: Using the new rule, the גמרא explains the argument about saying a ברכה when attaching ציצית. One view holds ציצית is an obligation on the garment, so attaching them completes the מצוה. The other holds it is an obligation on the person, so the מצוה is completed only when wearing it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And about ציצית, this is what they argue about: One sage holds it is an obligation on the garment, and one sage holds it is an obligation on the man.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא applies the new rule to explain an earlier argument about whether one says a ברכה when attaching ציצית to a garment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If ציצית is an obligation on the garment, then attaching them finishes the מצוה, like מילה, so a ברכה is said. If it is an obligation on the person, the מצוה is completed only when he wears the garment, like putting on תפילין, so attaching the ציצית gets no ברכה. These are the two opinions mentioned earlier: רב אדא בר אהבה, and רב נחמן quoting רב.

keyTerms.meaning: They disagree
An obligation on the garment
An obligation on the person
One sage holds

steps.whatToRemember: The question 'is ציצית a חוֹבַת טַלִּית or a חוֹבַת גַּבְרָא?' decides whether attaching ציצית completes the מצוה and so gets its own ברכה.
steps.whyThisMatters: The question of חוֹבַת טַלִּית versus חוֹבַת גַּבְרָא is a basic way of understanding the מצוה of ציצית, and it matters well beyond the question of a ברכה.

phrases.english: And regarding ritual fringes, in this they disagree:
phrases.notes: This is the earlier argument over whether to say a ברכה when attaching ציצית to a garment.

phrases.english: one sage holds it is an obligation of the garment,
and one sage holds it is an obligation of the man.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the principle from step 3 to explain the argument about ציצית.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The ציצית argument depends on whether ציצית is a חוֹבַת טַלִּית (attaching completes the מצוה, so a ברכה is said) or a חוֹבַת גַּבְרָא (only wearing completes it, so no ברכה on attaching).

steps.title: Another version of רב's teaching: ציצית made by a non-Jew are valid
steps.stepSummary: רב מרדכי tells רב אשי that in his tradition, רב taught that ציצית made by a גוי are valid. He learns this from the words 'ועשו להם'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מרדכי said to רב אשי: You learn רב's teaching one way. We learn it differently. רב יהודה said in the name of רב: How do we know that ציצית made by a גוי are valid? The פסוק says 'Speak to בני ישראל and they shall make for themselves ציצית.' This means others may make them for them.
steps.whatsHappening: רב מרדכי quotes a different version of רב's teaching. In his version, ציצית tied by a גוי are kosher.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי's version had רב saying a גוי's ציצית are invalid. רב מרדכי's version says the opposite, so there is no clash with רב's other teachings. He reads the word לָהֶם as 'for them,' which means someone else, even a גוי, may make ציצית for a Jew.

keyTerms.meaning: You teach / we teach: a way of saying 'this is the version we learned'
A non-Jew
Valid, kosher
Others may make them for them: reading לָהֶם as 'for them'

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with תפילין from step 1. There a גוי's writing is invalid. Here, in this version, a גוי's ציצית are valid, because the פסוק itself allows others to make them.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב מָרְדֳּכַי לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rav Mordechai said to Rav Ashi:
You teach it this way.
phrases.notes: He means the version where רב says ציצית made by a גוי are invalid.

phrases.english: We teach it this way:
Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
From where do we know that ציצית made by a gentile are valid?
For it is said:
"Speak to the children of Israel
and they shall make for themselves ציצית"
Others may make them for them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַתּוּן הָכִי מַתְנִיתוּ לַהּ, אֲנַן הָכִי מַתְנֵינַן לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different version of רב's teaching about ציצית made by a גוי.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב said that ציצית made by a גוי are invalid.
steps.terutzMaskana: In this version רב said that ציצית made by a גוי are valid, learned from 'ועשו להם'.
steps.raayaObject: ציצית made by a גוי are valid

steps.title: Which threads may be used for ציצית
steps.stepSummary: רב rules on threads used as ציצית. Threads sticking out of the garment, sewing threads, and hanging loose ends are invalid. Tufts of wool are valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: If someone made ציצית from threads sticking out of the cloth, or from leftover sewing threads, or from the loose ends hanging off the garment, they are invalid. If he made them from tufts of wool, they are valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling from רב about what materials are good for ציצית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first three kinds of thread were already part of the garment, and they were never made as ציצית. Loose tufts of wool are fine for רב, even though they were not spun for the מצוה. This sets up שמואל's disagreement in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Threads sticking out of the cloth like thorns
Sewing threads left on the garment
Loose thread-ends hanging from the edge of the garment
Tufts or swatches of wool
Invalid

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
If he made them from the protruding threads,
or from the sewing threads,
or from the hanging loose ends, it is invalid.
If from tufts of wool, it is valid.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב: עֲשָׂאָן מִן הַקּוֹצִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: which threads are kosher for ציצית.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Threads already on the garment are invalid as ציצית. Tufts of wool are valid.

steps.title: שמואל: the thread must be spun for the מצוה
steps.stepSummary: שמואל disagrees with רב about tufts of wool. He holds they are also invalid, because the spinning must be done for the sake of the מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה says: When I said this before שמואל, he said: Even tufts of wool are invalid, because we need the thread to be spun for the sake of the מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה reports that שמואל rejected part of רב's ruling, the part about tufts of wool.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב only required that the ציצית be made from separate thread, not from threads already on the garment. שמואל adds a stricter rule: the spinning of the thread itself must be לשמה. So tufts that were not spun for the מצוה are also invalid.

keyTerms.meaning: Spinning, making wool into thread
For its sake: done for the purpose of the מצוה
Even

steps.whatToRemember: רב: tufts of wool are valid for ציצית. שמואל: they are invalid, because the thread must be spun לשמה, for the מצוה.

phrases.english: When I said it before Shmuel,
phrases.notes: The speaker is רב יהודה, telling over רב's ruling.

phrases.english: he said: Even from tufts of wool it is invalid,
we require spinning for its sake.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אַמְרִיתַהּ קַמֵּיהּ דִּשְׁמוּאֵל, אָמַר: אַף מִן הַסִּיסִין פְּסוּלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: שמואל rejects the last part of רב's ruling from step 6.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only רב's ruling that tufts of wool are valid
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: שמואל holds that the thread must be spun לשמה, while רב does not require this.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Tufts of wool not spun לשמה are also invalid for ציצית, because the spinning must be for the sake of the מצוה.

steps.title: The Argument Matches an Older Argument Between תנאים
steps.stepSummary: The argument between רב and שמואל about whether preparation must be לשמה matches a ברייתא about patching תפילין with leather. The תנא קמא says the leather does not need to be processed לשמה. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says it does.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is like an argument between תנאים. If someone coated תפילין with gold, or patched them with the skin of a non-kosher animal, they are invalid. If he patched them with the skin of a kosher animal, they are valid, even if he did not process the leather לשמה. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says that even with the skin of a kosher animal they are invalid, until he processes it לשמה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that the argument between רב and שמואל about preparing wool לשמה is really an older argument between תנאים about processing leather for תפילין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא accepts kosher leather even if it was not processed לשמה, like רב, who accepts tufts of wool. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל requires processing לשמה, like שמואל, who requires spinning לשמה. So both opinions already have support from a ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: Like an argument between תנאים: this later argument matches an older one.
He coated them, meaning covered the תפילין.
A non-kosher animal.
He processed (tanned) the leather.
For their sake, meaning done for the purpose of the מצוה.

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the question of preparing materials לשמה is not new with רב and שמואל. It goes back to the time of the תנאים.

phrases.english: This is like an argument between תנאים:
phrases.notes: The תנא קמא below holds like רב, and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל holds like שמואל.

phrases.english: If he coated them with gold,
phrases.notes: "Them" means תפילין. The ברייתא is talking about the outer covering of the תפילין boxes.

phrases.english: or if he patched onto them
the skin of a non-kosher animal, they are invalid.
With the skin of a kosher animal, they are valid,

phrases.aramaic: וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא עִיבְּדָן לִשְׁמָן.
phrases.english: even though he did not process it for their sake.
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
Even with the skin of a kosher animal, they are invalid,
until he processes it for their sake.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Connects the argument between רב and שמואל in steps 6-7 to an older argument between תנאים.
steps.raayaObject: The argument between רב and שמואל about whether preparation for a מצוה must be לשמה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about patching תפילין with leather, where the תנא קמא and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל argue about processing לשמה.

steps.title: אביי Asks How תכלת Is Dyed
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks רב שמואל בר רב יהודה how they dye the תכלת wool for ציצית.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to רב שמואל בר רב יהודה: How do you dye this תכלת?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new section with a practical question about dyeing תכלת. This question sets up a description that the גמרא will learn rules from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי is asking for the actual method used in practice. The details of the answer will show how they treated dyeing as a step done for the מצוה.

keyTerms.meaning: תכלת: the sky-blue wool used in ציצית.
You (plural) dye.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי לְרַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר רַב יְהוּדָה:
phrases.english: Abaye said to Rav Shmuel bar Rav Yehuda:
This sky-blue wool, how do you dye it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic about dyeing תכלת, which connects to the theme of preparing materials לשמה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The practical method used to dye תכלת.

steps.title: The Method of Dyeing תכלת
steps.stepSummary: They boil the חלזון blood with herbs in a pot. They take a little of the dye in an eggshell and test it on a wad of wool. Then they throw away the eggshell and burn the test wool.
steps.simpleTranslation: He answered: We bring blood of the חלזון and herbs and put them in a pot. We take a little in an eggshell and test it on a wad of wool. Then we throw away that eggshell and burn the wad of wool.
steps.whatsHappening: רב שמואל בר רב יהודה describes the dyeing process step by step, including how they test the color.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two details stand out. The testing is done with dye taken out into a separate eggshell, not in the main pot. Afterward, both the test dye and the test wool are destroyed. The גמרא will learn rules from these details in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: The sea creature whose blood is used to make תכלת dye.
Herbs or other ingredients added to the dye.
A large pot for boiling.
An egg, here meaning an eggshell used as a small container.
A wad or tuft of wool.

phrases.english: He said to him:
We bring blood of the חלזון and herbs,
and we put them into a pot,
and we take a little in an egg,
phrases.notes: He means an eggshell, used as a small cup to hold a little of the dye.

phrases.english: and we test it on a wad of wool,
phrases.notes: Literally "we taste it." He means they try the dye on some wool to check the color.

phrases.english: and we throw away that egg,
and we burn the wad of wool.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The dyeing method: boil the dye, test a separate small amount on wool, then throw away the test dye and burn the test wool.

steps.title: Three Rules Learned From the Dyeing Method
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא learns three rules from this method. Test-dyed wool is invalid, dyeing must be לשמה, and testing in the dye makes that dye invalid.
steps.simpleTranslation: Learn three things from this. Learn that test-dyed wool is invalid. Learn that we need dyeing לשמה. And learn that testing makes the dye invalid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws three rules from the details of the dyeing method.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The test wool is burned, which shows that wool dyed only as a test is invalid. This shows that dyeing must be לשמה. The test is done in a separate eggshell, which shows that testing in the dye would ruin the dye itself, so they keep the main pot away from it.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from it: the גמרא is drawing a rule from what was just said.
Testing: literally "tasting," meaning trying the dye on wool.
Dyeing done for the sake of the מצוה.
It makes something invalid.

steps.confusionAlert: Notice the small difference between the first and third rules. פְּסוּלָה means the tested wool is invalid. פָּסְלָה means the testing makes the dye itself invalid.

phrases.english: Learn three things from this:
Learn from it that test-dyed wool is invalid,
and learn from it that we need dyeing for its sake,
and learn from it that testing makes the dye invalid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws rules from the dyeing method described in step 10.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Test-dyed wool is invalid, dyeing must be לשמה, and testing in the dye makes that dye invalid.

steps.title: Aren't Two of the Rules the Same?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the first two rules are counted separately. Test-dyed wool is invalid only because dyeing must be לשמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But "test-dyed wool is invalid" is the same as "dyeing must be לשמה"!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the count of three. It says the first two rules seem to be one rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wool dyed as a test is invalid only because it was not dyed for the מצוה. So the two rules seem to say the same thing. That would leave only two rules, not three.

keyTerms.meaning: That is the same as: used to say two things are really one.

phrases.english: Test-dyed wool being invalid,
is that not the same as dyeing for its sake?

steps.triggerLanguage: הַיְינוּ טְעִימָה פְּסוּלָה, הַיְינוּ צְבִיעָה לִשְׁמָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the count of three rules from step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 11 that three separate rules are learned.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The first two rules have the same cause, so they should count as one.

steps.title: רב אשי: The Second Rule Is the Reason for the First
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי explains that the גמרא was not listing a separate rule. It was giving the reason: test-dyed wool is invalid because dyeing must be לשמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: It is saying "what is the reason." Why is test-dyed wool invalid? Because we need dyeing לשמה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers the challenge. He says the second line explains the first line and is not a new rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words "we need dyeing לשמה" give the reason why test-dyed wool is invalid. So the first two lines go together as one rule with its reason. The third rule, that testing makes the dye invalid, stays as a separate point.

keyTerms.meaning: It is saying "what is the reason": the second part explains the first and is not a new point.

steps.whatToRemember: Wool for תכלת must be dyed לשמה. That is why test-dyed wool is invalid and is burned, and why they test with dye taken out of the main pot.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
It is saying "what is the reason":
What is the reason that test-dyed wool is invalid?
Because we need dyeing for its sake.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading the text differently: the second line is the reason for the first, not a separate rule.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The first two lines were two separate rules that say the same thing.
steps.terutzMaskana: The second line explains the first. Test-dyed wool is invalid because dyeing must be לשמה.

steps.title: Tested dye is invalid, according to רבי חנינא בן גמליאל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the rule that testing makes the dye invalid is a dispute between תנאים. The first view, from רבי חנינא בן גמליאל, holds that tested dye is invalid, based on the words כליל תכלת.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is a dispute between תנאים. Dye that was used for testing is invalid, because the פסוק says 'כליל תכלת'. These are the words of רבי חנינא בן גמליאל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the third rule from step 11 is not agreed on by everyone. It is a dispute between תנאים, and here is the first side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חנינא בן גמליאל reads כליל, 'entirely', to mean the dye must be used fully and only for its proper purpose. Dye that was already used for a test is no longer 'whole', so it is invalid.

keyTerms.meaning: This matches a dispute between תנאים
Literally 'tasting'. Here it means dye that was used for a test.
Invalid, not usable for the מצוה
'Entirely of תכלת', from the פסוק about the מעיל

phrases.english: It is like a dispute between תנאים:
Dye used for testing is invalid,
because it says: 'entirely of תכלת',
These are the words of רבי חנינא בן גמליאל.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ties the third rule from step 11 to a dispute between תנאים
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Dye that was used for testing is invalid for תכלת, because of the word כליל.

steps.title: Even a second use of the dye is valid, according to רבי יוחנן בן דהבאי
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן בן דהבאי disagrees. He says even a second dyeing from the same dye is valid, based on the word שני in 'ושני תולעת'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן בן דהבאי says: even a second use of the dye is valid, because the פסוק says 'ושני תולעת'.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the other side of the dispute. רבי יוחנן בן דהבאי allows dye that was already used once.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He plays on the word שני. It can mean 'scarlet', but it also sounds like 'second'. From this he learns that a second use of the dye is acceptable, so testing does not ruin the dye.

keyTerms.meaning: A 'second appearance', meaning the color from a second use of the dye
Valid, usable
Scarlet wool. The word שני also sounds like 'second'.

steps.whatToRemember: The rule that tested dye becomes invalid is a dispute. רבי חנינא בן גמליאל says it is invalid (כליל). רבי יוחנן בן דהבאי says even a second use is valid (שני).

phrases.english: רבי יוחנן בן דהבאי says:
Even a second coloring from it is valid,
because it says: 'and scarlet wool'.
phrases.notes: ויקרא 14:4. The word שני can also be read as 'second'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing view to step 14
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even a second use of the dye is valid, so testing does not make the dye invalid.

steps.title: Which items can be checked and who may sell them
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא compares three groups. תכלת cannot be checked and must be bought from a מומחה. תפילין can be checked but must still come from a מומחה. ספרים and מזוזות can be checked and may be bought from anyone.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: תכלת has no way to be checked, so it is bought only from a מומחה. תפילין can be checked, but they are bought only from a מומחה. ספרים and מזוזות can be checked, and they may be bought from anyone.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא about buying תכלת and other holy items. It explains whose word we may trust for each one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For תכלת, there is no test to tell real תכלת from fake, so we must rely on an expert seller. תפילין can be checked, yet a מומחה is still required. ספרים and מזוזות can be checked, so anyone may sell them.

keyTerms.meaning: A way to check or test that something is valid
An expert, a trusted professional
ספרי תורה and מזוזות

phrases.aramaic: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: תְּכֵלֶת אֵין לָהּ בְּדִיקָה,
phrases.english: The רבנן taught: תכלת has no way to be checked,
and it may be bought only from an expert.
תפילין do have a way to be checked,
yet they may be bought only from an expert.
Torah scrolls and מזוזות have a way to be checked,
and they may be bought from anyone.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: תְּכֵלֶת אֵין לָהּ בְּדִיקָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: checking תכלת and trusting sellers
steps.mimraCoreRuling: תכלת cannot be checked, so it may be bought only from a מומחה.

steps.title: But רב יצחק did check תכלת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא. If תכלת cannot be checked, how did רב יצחק בריה דרב יהודה check it?
steps.simpleTranslation: Does תכלת really have no way to be checked? But רב יצחק, the son of רב יהודה, used to check it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the first line of the ברייתא. It points to an אמורא who actually performed a test on תכלת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says no test exists for תכלת. A real-life case of someone checking it seems to show that a test does exist. This contradiction must be resolved.

keyTerms.meaning: 'But surely...', which opens a challenge from a known fact
He checked or tested

phrases.english: And does תכלת really have no way to be checked?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא רַב יִצְחָק בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוּדָה
phrases.english: But רב יצחק, the son of רב יהודה,
used to check it!

steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that תכלת אין לה בדיקה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב יצחק בריה דרב יהודה actually tested תכלת, so a test must exist.

steps.title: The start of רב יצחק's test for תכלת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a memory hint and begins listing the materials רב יצחק used for his test: alum clay, fenugreek water, and urine. The description continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: (Memory hint: ג, ש, מ.) He would bring alum clay, fenugreek water, and urine...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is spelling out how רב יצחק did his test, to support the challenge in step 17. The sentence is not finished here and continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Listing the actual ingredients shows that this was a real, working test. That makes the challenge to 'תכלת has no test' stronger. The memory hint helps the learner remember the three ingredients.

keyTerms.meaning: A memory hint to help remember a list
Alum clay
Fenugreek, a plant
Urine

phrases.english: (Memory hint: ג, ש, מ)
phrases.notes: A memory hint for the three ingredients: ג for גילא, ש for שבלילתא, מ for מימי. Some versions leave it out.

phrases.english: He would bring alum clay,
and fenugreek water,
and urine

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the test that was the basis for the challenge in step 17
steps.raayaObject: That a test for תכלת does exist
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב יצחק בריה דרב יהודה's actual testing method
